title: An experiment to make a highly fun FOSS game with the community using AI.
author: 1kmile
selftext:
AI is achieving capable feats everywhere - mostly because researchers are pushing its boundaries. We want to push the boundaries in our way. No one can individually spawn thousands of agents. But a community can. We can let our agents coordinate with each other.



This project is in its most earliest stage. There's no clear idea of what game engine we will use, nor what even is the game about. This is mostly the human part.



We are discussing it in the discord server.

[https://discord.gg/wJjjf5SGS5](https://discord.gg/wJjjf5SGS5)



After we decide the game idea and engine. We will figure out our workflow step by step. What matters is getting started





Let's do something impressive and owned by the community.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
> No one can individually spawn thousands of agents. But a community can.

The point if digital AI is that everyone can spawn thousands of agents, they are digital and cheap.

>highly fun FOSS game with the community

Every few months we see this pitch in some game development community, the simple fact is it goes like school group projects. You have a few people working and the others just standing around doing nothing. It has been tried a million times and failed.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
> FOSS game with the community

This will not go well. For FOSS, it usually starts as a one person implementing their vision and other people contribute a little. So it's like, 90% of owner's direction and 10% accepted community ideas. And those 10% are usually from the people, whose vision matches the vision of owner. People see the end goal in the same way, that makes them complete the thing. And if it has 0 contributors, the core guy continues working on it

If you start with no end goal - people might get bored and run away. So maybe you should make the idea, i.e. "we make first and only, microbiotic dress up game, join and contribute to FOSS". This will be more engaging then "abstract FOSS, no engine"

replies.author: Western-Movie9890
replies.body: even the idea alone is often not enough to build some community, you need some basic working version
